source: Publisher documentation saved under e3/truth/docs/fresh/ (sha256 in SHA256SUMS): TPC-DS v3.2.0; LDBC SNB specification (v2.2.5-SNAPSHOT, Appendix D for the Interactive v1 legacy data sets); GTFS Schedule Reference; FAA ardata.pdf (5/8/2025); ABS ASGS Edition 3 web pages; SEC Financial Statement Data Sets; College Scorecard Field of Study documentation (October 2026) and data dictionary; EPA AirData FileFormats (v3.0.0); 2024 ACS PUMS data dictionary and Census regions and divisions; City of Chicago portal metadata (ijzp-q8t2, c7ck-438e); USDA FoodData Central download field descriptions (October 2020)
rule: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the confirmatory evaluation, joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: TPC-DS v3.2.0 schema, data from dsdgen 2.10.0 (gregrahn/tpcds-kit) at scale factor 1 with the default seed: customer (root; 100,000 rows at 1GB per Table 3-2) left-joined to customer_address on c_current_addr_sk, customer_demographics on c_current_cdemo_sk, household_demographics on c_current_hdemo_sk and income_band on hd_income_band_sk; to stay within 25 columns the date keys, free-text and secondary columns were dropped (c_first_shipto_date_sk, c_first_sales_date_sk, c_salutation, c_preferred_cust_flag, c_birth_day, c_birth_month, c_birth_year, c_login, c_email_address, c_last_review_date_sk, ca_address_id, ca_street_number, ca_street_name, ca_street_type, ca_suite_number, ca_country, ca_location_type, hd_dep_count, hd_vehicle_count), the surrogate keys ca_address_sk, cd_demo_sk, hd_demo_sk and ib_income_band_sk are represented by the foreign-key columns that equal them, and all eight demographic columns are kept so that their documented key survives.

cleaning.missing_values: empty and missing references become '?', kept as a value (null = null)

truth.clause: tpc-ds_v3.2.0.pdf, Clause 2.4.7, Table 2-14 (p. 32): "Each row in this dimension table represents a customer." and "c_customer_sk identifier N Y"; tpc-ds_v3.2.0.pdf, Clause 2.2.1.2 (p. 22): "Columns that are part of the table's primary key are indicated in the column called Primary Key"
truth.justification: c_customer_sk is the declared primary key of customer, and the right-hand side are columns of customer.

audit.quote: c_customer_sk identifier N Y | A Primary Key is one or more columns that uniquely identifies a row.
audit.source: tpc-ds_v3.2.0.pdf, Clause 2.4.7, Table 2-14, p. 32; tpc-ds_v3.2.0.pdf, Clause 2.5.1.6, p. 36

truth.clause: tpc-ds_v3.2.0.pdf, Table 2-14 (p. 32): "c_current_addr_sk identifier ca_addres_sk"; Clause 2.4.8, Table 2-15 (p. 32): "ca_address_sk identifier N Y"; tpc-ds_v3.2.0.pdf, Clause 2.2.4 (p. 23): "If the values in this column join with another column, the foreign columns name is listed in the Foreign Key field of the column definition."
truth.justification: c_current_addr_sk is a foreign key to the declared primary key ca_address_sk of customer_address, so it determines the columns of the one address row it references; the documented 'each customer can have more than one address' concerns the rows of customer_address, not the single current address of a customer row.

truth.clause: tpc-ds_v3.2.0.pdf, Clause 2.2.1.3 (p. 22): "A business key is neither a primary key nor a foreign key in the context of the data warehouse schema. It is only used to differentiate new data from update data of the source tables during the data maintenance operations."; Clause 1.3.3 (p. 18): "As dimension rows are updated, the previous values are overwritten and this information is lost." and "Customer is an example of a Non-Historical dimension."
truth.justification: c_customer_id is the business key (B) of customer, and a non-historical dimension overwrites a row instead of adding one, so one row per business key follows; the specification never states that c_customer_id is unique, and it says a business key is not a key of the schema, hence unsure.

audit.quote: Historical: The history of the changes made to the dimension data is maintained by creating multiple rows for a single business key value. ... Non-Historical: The history of the changes made to the dimension data is not maintained. As dimension rows are updated, the previous values are overwritten and this information is lost. ... Customer is an example of a Non-Historical dimension. | It is only used to differentiate new data from update data of the source tables during the data maintenance operations. | LEFT OUTER JOIN customer ON (purc_customer_id = c_customer_id)
audit.source: tpc-ds_v3.2.0.pdf, Clause 1.3.3, p. 18; Clause 2.2.1.3, p. 22; Clause 5.3.11.1 (view ssv), p. 58

gold_design_note: No normalized design is published; the 3NF designs of Sigma* are synthesized.

mined.algorithm: fdmine.py: exact discovery of all minimal FDs in the style of HyFD (no HyFD binary was available); the complete set of minimal FDs is unique, so it equals HyFD's output
